thread.title: PPI: No Persecution, Just Accountability

author: gmanews
title: PPI: No Persecution, Just Accountability
text: PPI: No Persecution, Just Accountability The Planters Products Inc. (PPI) refutes claims of persecution against former Agriculture secretary Leonardo Montemayor, stating the cyberlibel charges are grounded in factual evidence of defamation. The case revolves around Montemayor's accusations regarding PPI's corporate status and rice importation practices, which PPI denies, asserting its private nature and adherence to legal standards. The Planters Products Inc. (PPI) has defended itself against allegations of persecution following the indictment of former Agriculture secretary Leonardo Montemayor for cyberlibel. The charges stem from Montemayor's claims that PPI is a government-owned corporation (GOCC) and his criticism of the company's importation of about 22,750 metric tons of rice from Vietnam. PPI asserts that it is a private entity with shares owned by individuals and private companies, not the government. The Makati City Prosecutor's Office found prima facie evidence of defamation in Montemayor's statements, leading to an arrest warrant and a scheduled arraignment. While Montemayor and his supporters claim the charges are an attempt to silence critics, PPI's legal counsel argues the case is about distinguishing truth from falsehood and upholding the law against defamation.
